**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN).**

- **What exists:** Article XIV gives us a RevMed indemnity (§14.1) for RevMed's negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, breach of its reps and warranties, and breach of its obligations, with a full standard procedure (notice, control of defence, participation, settlement consent, cooperation, expense reimbursement) in §14.3, and §14.5 confirms the consequential-damages waiver does not cut back indemnities. Our own indemnity (§14.2) is properly confined to our Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization conduct and our breaches.
- **Gap:** no head of indemnity for third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. That risk sits with us via §14.2(a), and is only indirectly reachable through the knowledge-qualified, Execution-Date IP warranties (§13.2(f)–(g)); §10.7 merely gives us a first right to buy a third-party licence at our own cost. Per the detection guidance, a Vendor indemnity excluding IP infringement fails the fallback.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new §14.1(d) adding an express RevMed IP infringement indemnity (notwithstanding §14.2(a)), plus the consequential cross-reference fix in the existing proviso — RevMed's carve-outs for our negligence and breaches remain unchanged.
